title: Total Ordering of Resources: A Quantum-Classical Separation
authors: Jingsong Ao, Julio I. de Vicente, Alexander Streltsov
abstract: A central goal in quantum information science is understanding which physical states can be converted into others. The ideal scenario would be a totally ordered system, where every state can be ranked by a single value, and a higher-ranked state can always be converted into a lower-ranked one. Such an ordering would provide a complete description of state convertibility, making the resource structure maximally simple to characterize and compare. We prove that such a simple ordering is fundamentally impossible for any quantum system with dimension larger than 2. The underlying properties of quantum mechanics guarantee that some states will always be incomparable. Furthermore, we show this is a uniquely quantum phenomenon by constructing classical systems of any size that can be perfectly ranked. This establishes a rigorous and striking divide between quantum and classical state transformations.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that quantum resource theories in dimensions three or higher cannot be totally ordered, meaning there will always exist pairs of quantum states that cannot be ranked relative to each other. This impossibility is a unique feature of quantum mechanics, as classical systems of any size can always be perfectly ranked. The result establishes a rigorous mathematical divide between quantum and classical state transformation capabilities.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether quantum resource theories can be characterized by a single, total ordering of states, which would simplify the understanding of state convertibility.
main_result: It proves that for quantum systems of dimension $d \geq 3$, such a total ordering is fundamentally impossible due to the existence of incomparable states. This property is shown to be a purely quantum phenomenon.
method: The authors use structural proofs by contradiction, analyzing the properties of resource monotones and leveraging convexity arguments on the state space to demonstrate the existence of incomparable states.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum resource theories defined over the space of density operators ($\mathcal{D}_d$) on a $d$-dimensional quantum system. The analysis contrasts these quantum systems with classical systems.
key_observables: Resource monotone ($M$), the existence of incomparable states ($ho, \sigma$), and the dimension ($d$) of the system.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ (specifically $d \geq 3$), and the structure of the free set ($F$) and allowed operations ($\mathcal{O}_F$).
main_assumptions: The resource theory is non-trivial, and the analysis focuses on deterministic, unassisted state transformations.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the goal of total ordering, proves the impossibility for $d \geq 3$ quantum systems (Theorem 1), and contrasts this impossibility with the fact that classical resource theories *can* be totally ordered in any finite dimension.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental mathematical constraint on the structure of quantum resources, establishing a clear boundary between quantum and classical physics in the context of state transformation theory.
